name: Meal Planner
description: The family's meals for the week, day by day, with the groceries for them ordered on the family's grocery app, the everyday items and the family's recipe book; not for school runs, chores or appointments.

for: The family's meals for the week: Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, day by day, each with its dishes
Groceries for the week's meals, ordered on the family's grocery app when they are needed
Everyday items (milk, curd, bread) ordered again and again on their own
The family's saved recipes, with their videos, planned into the week
notFor: School runs, chores or appointments (use checklist or tracker)
Keeping count of what is in the kitchen
A restaurant's menu or a business kitchen

settings.label: The grocery app orders go to

routines.name: Weekly meal plan
routines.description: Once a week, asks the agent to plan next week's meals, place the week's first order and send the family the plan with one question about what is low or out. On an install carried over from the old Meal Planner it first asks for the family's profile to be structured.

routines.name: Dinner check-in
routines.description: Every afternoon, sends the family tonight's dinner and whether its fresh items are on an order. Silent when no dinner is planned or it is ordered in. The time it runs at is the time the app tells the family.

routines.name: Tomorrow's meals check-in
routines.description: Every evening, sends the family tomorrow's meals, with the dishes' videos for the cook on the days they come. Silent when nothing is planned. The time it runs at is the time the app tells the family.

routines.name: Order clock
routines.description: Every 15 minutes, hands the agent each grocery order whose time has come, to place it. No model call unless an order is due.

operations.name: guide
operations.description: The full guide for working with this app: read it before the first conversation, a weekly plan, a check-in or an order. {}

operations.name: set_person
operations.description: Add or change one person who eats at home, found by name. { name, relationship?, group?: child | adult | elder, portions?, diet?, allergies?, dislikes?, targets?, note?, remove?: true }. group is needed for a new person. Keep portions, diet and the rest in the family's own words. Only the fields you send change; null clears one; remove: true takes the person out of the family.

operations.name: set_house_rules
operations.description: The house's food rules; the list you send replaces the one there. { rules?: [{ kind: veg | egg | fasting | no_onion_garlic | other, days: ["Tue", "Thu"], note? }], notes?, structured?: true }. Send at least one of the three. A rule needs its days: weekdays, or the family's own word for a day ("Ekadashi"). Send structured: true once a profile carried over from the old app is fully in people, rules, the cook and slots, and at least one person is saved: it clears that text.

operations.name: set_cook
operations.description: The cook: who, which days, when they arrive, what they make well. { name, days: ["Mon", ...], arrival: "HH:MM", makes_well?, note? }. name, days and arrival are needed every time.

operations.name: set_slots
operations.description: Meals beyond Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner, and the meals the family orders in every week. { extra_slots?: [{ name, days?: ["Mon", ...], for?: [names] }], order_in?: [{ day: "Sun", slot: "Dinner", note? }] }. Send at least one of the two; each list you send replaces the one there. An order_in slot is Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or an extra slot's name.

operations.name: plan_week
operations.description: Plan a week of meals. { week_start: the week's Monday as YYYY-MM-DD, mode: draft | final, meals?: [{ date, slot, ordered_in?: true, note?, dishes?: [{ name, for?: [names], portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit?, keeps?: fresh | long }] }] }] }. Without meals it answers with the context to plan from (people, house, everyday items, last week's dishes, the recipe book), or, when mode is final and the week is a draft, makes that draft final. With meals they become the whole week's plan, in place of what was there. A draft with meals is refused once the week has orders: change a meal with set_meal or set_dish, or send mode final with the new meals. A dish is for everyone unless you name who it is for; amount is a number above 0 with its measure in unit, for this family; an ordered-in meal has no dishes. Answers { week } or { context }; a final plan also answers with orders: the week's orders, built from it (fresh items in the order covering their day, long-life ones in the first).

operations.name: set_meal
operations.description: Change one meal, found by date and slot (or meal_id) and made when it is not there. { date, slot, or meal_id; ordered_in?, note?, dishes?: [as in plan_week] }. Only what you send changes; dishes you send replace the meal's dishes. ordered_in: true takes its dishes away; sending dishes with it is refused, and a meal that is ordered in takes dishes only with ordered_in: false. A meal keeps its date and slot. Answers { meal }.

operations.name: set_dish
operations.description: Add, change or remove one dish. { dish_id, or meal_id, or date and slot; name?, for?: [names], portion_note?, recipe_id?, video_url?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit?, keeps? }], position?, remove?: true }. Without dish_id, name is needed: in that meal a dish of the same name is the one changed; otherwise it is added at the end (and the meal made when it is not there). By dish_id a name you send renames it. Only what you send changes; ingredients you send replace the dish's; position 0 is first; for: null means everyone. Answers { dish, meal }.

operations.name: set_regular
operations.description: Add or change one everyday item: what the house buys again and again whatever is cooked (milk, curd, bread, eggs). { item, amount, unit, every: day | week | weekdays, times_per_week?, weekdays?: ["Mon", ...], for_whom?, keeps?: fresh | long, active?, paused_until?: YYYY-MM-DD, remove?: true }. amount (a number above 0), unit and every are needed for a new item. amount is what is needed each time: 1 l every day; 1 pack with every: week and times_per_week: 2; 6 pc with every: weekdays and weekdays: ["Mon"]. times_per_week is a whole number from 1 to 7 (1 when left out); weekdays is needed, with at least one day, when every is weekdays. Found by item and for_whom; only the fields you send change. paused_until leaves it out of the orders up to and including that date (a holiday); active: false stops it until you send active: true; remove: true deletes it. Set one only after the family confirmed it.

operations.name: import_order_history
operations.description: Give the app the family's past orders on a grocery app. { app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, orders: [{ date: YYYY-MM-DD, items: [{ item, qty?, pack?, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }] }] }. item is the product's name as the order has it. Every item sent with its product_id is remembered as a product under that name. Answers { suggestions: [{ item, amount, unit, every: day | week, times_per_week?, orders_seen }] }: what was bought on three or more days, at least once a fortnight; amount is the usual number of packs in an order and unit the usual pack. It makes no everyday item itself: ask the family about each suggestion, set_regular the ones they confirm, and remember_product each one's product again under the item's own name.

operations.name: remember_product
operations.description: Remember the product an item is bought as on a grocery app, so the next order reuses it without searching. { item, app: zepto | swiggy-instamart | zomato-blinkit | bigbasket, product_id, name_on_app, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. item is the family's word for it, exactly as on the order line or the everyday item (milk), never the product's name on the app; pack_amount and pack_unit are the pack's size as a number and its measure (500, ml), which the app counts packs with (a plain pack text like "500 ml" is read too). One product per item and app: sending it again takes the place of the one remembered. Answers { product }.

operations.name: save_recipe
operations.description: Save a recipe, or change one. { recipe_id?, name?, links?: [the reel, short or page], notes?, ingredients?: [{ item, amount?, unit? }], tags?: ["breakfast", "tiffin"], for?: [names], thumbnail? }. Without recipe_id, a recipe that already holds one of the links is the one changed (new links are added to it), so a link shared twice is saved once; otherwise a new recipe is made, and it needs a name: with none the answer is code NEEDS_NAME, so ask the family what to call it and save again. By recipe_id only what you send changes, and links you send replace its links. Answers { recipe }; put its id on a dish with set_dish recipe_id.

operations.name: ask_low_or_out
operations.description: The week's long-life items (atta, rice, dal, oil), to ask the family about once. { week_start, low_or_out?: [items] }. Without low_or_out it answers { order_id, items, question }: send the question ("Atta, rice, toor dal: any low or out?") with the plan. When they answer, send as low_or_out the names from items that they said are low or out, spelt as items has them ([] when they have everything): names are matched by word, so a misspelt one reads as an item they have. The items named stay ordered; the rest are taken off the week's next scheduled order as things they have. An order already placed is never changed; an item that is out and on no order goes on the next scheduled one, or on a new order to place now. Answers { order }. Nothing about what is at home is kept beyond that order.

operations.name: add_to_order
operations.description: Add one item to an order. { order_id?, item, qty?, product_id?, name_on_app?, pack?, pack_amount?, pack_unit?, price?, image? }. Without order_id it goes on the next scheduled order, or on a new order to place now when none is waiting; an order that is not scheduled is refused. item is the family's word for it (coriander), never the product's name on the app; qty is a whole number of packs (1 when left out). Send the product the family picked (product_id and name_on_app, with its pack and price) and it is remembered as that item's product; without one the item's remembered product is used. Answers { order, line }.

operations.name: place_order
operations.description: Call just before you place a scheduled order on the grocery app. { order_id }. Answers { order, message, needs_product, needs_qty }: send message to the family first, word for word; needs_product are the lines with no remembered product (find each on the grocery app); needs_qty are the lines whose number of packs the app could not work out from the pack size (work each out); the guide says how to save both. Then place the order without waiting for a yes, and record_order at once. An order that is not scheduled, or has nothing on it, is refused.

operations.name: record_order
operations.description: Record what happened to an order on the grocery app. { order_id, placed?: true | false, paid?: true | false, total?, app_order_ref?, note? }. Send placed or paid. placed: true once it is placed and waiting for the person's payment; placed: false with a note when it could not be placed (it stays scheduled and is tried again). paid: true once the payment went through; paid: false when it was not paid, or they said cancel: the order is closed as not paid and its items move to the next scheduled order (or a new one), named in rolled_into; cancel nothing on the grocery app. Only a scheduled order is recorded placed, only a placed one paid or not paid. When the answer has intro, send it to the family word for word.

operations.name: cancel_order
operations.description: Cancel an order. { order_id }. A scheduled order is cancelled. A placed order that is not yet paid is closed as not paid and its items move to the next order (rolled_into); cancel nothing on the grocery app. A paid order is refused: the person cancels it in the grocery app itself.

agentInterface.instructions: Meal Planner owns this family's profile, meals, everyday items, grocery orders and recipes. Read the app before you answer and change it only through its operations, then tell the family what the app now says. Call guide before a first conversation, a weekly plan, a check-in or an order. Save the family's own words; never fill anything from guesses. An order goes scheduled → placed (waiting for payment) → paid, or not paid. Placing needs no yes: send the app's message as it is, then place the order; the payment step asks the person. When they pay: record_order { paid: true }. If they do not pay, or say cancel: record_order { paid: false } or cancel_order. Nothing is cancelled on the grocery app (never call a connector's cancel): the order is marked not paid and its items move to the next order. A paid order is cancelled by the person in the grocery app itself. To add an item, search the grocery app and answer with the ItemPicker block (the numbered text on WhatsApp), then add_to_order. A shared reel plus "save this" is a save_recipe call.
